sections.title: Where did all the minimalists go?

items.q: What should you remember about **Cultural movements ≠ systemic reform**?
items.a: **minimalism inspired millions to declutter** and find purpose; inequality, captured state, and monopoly power need structural fixes.

items.q: What should you remember about **Inequality is an under-discussed consumption driver**?
items.a: **more equal societies (Japan, much of** Europe) show less status consumption and debt; US is extreme on both axes.

items.q: What should you remember about **Post-COVID consumerism spike**?
items.a: **isolation + social-media addiction + fractured social** circles → "injection" of spending; Levi Hildebrand: ~10× in a decade, exponential after COVID.

items.q: What should you remember about **Two reasons minimalism faded from headlines**?
items.a: **(1) viral moment novelty expired** (practice continues quietly), (2) polycrisis crowds out overconsumption as top worry.

items.q: What should you remember about **Voluntary vs compelled minimalism**?
items.a: **choosing less while able to afford more** ≠ being forced into scarcity; both are reactions to unfair outcomes, not the root problem.

items.q: What should you remember about **Hammer not religion**?
items.a: **minimalism creates tangible returns** (less cleaning, mental clutter) vs abstract sustainability pitches (bamboo toothbrush).

items.q: What should you remember about **Apathy purchases**?
items.a: **when systems feel broken,** habitual comfort spending (Stanley, Starbucks) soothes distress without fixing causes.

items.q: What should you remember about **Policy two-track**?
items.a: **progressive taxation/redistribution *plus* fairer** pre-tax market outcomes (unions, community power, break up monopolies).

items.q: What should you remember about **Historical optimism**?
items.a: **Schor**: crises often precede new structures (Great Depression → New Deal); enough pain eventually triggers "enough's enough".
